title: Swapping capslock/ctrl causes false pen actions on Surface Laptop Studio
author: notuntoward

status.label: Surface pen false-input reproduction is ready
status.detail: Docking or undocking a Surface pen toggles Caps Lock and can invoke Screen Snip only when the CapsLock/Ctrl remap is enabled. The reporter reproduced on two Surface generations, and maintainers intentionally separated this false-action issue from the related remapping issue.

next_action.label: Capture the Surface pen event sequence
next_action.reason: Reproduce on Surface hardware before selecting an injected-event or remap-state fix.

judgment.rationale: The public steps and hardware comparison are concrete, and disabling Keyboard Manager removes the behavior. The remaining discriminator is the actual keyboard/input sequence emitted by pen docking and how Keyboard Manager transforms it.
evidence: The original Surface Laptop Studio report includes a screenshot of the CapsLock/Ctrl swap and a diagnostic ZIP.
The reporter later reproduced different but related behavior on a Copilot Surface Pro.
Turning Keyboard Manager off stops the Caps Lock toggles and Screen Snip popup.
A maintainer says issue 33968 has the same visible symptoms but a distinct Win+Ctrl+F20 remapping failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a hardware-backed event trace and keep this issue separate from issue 33968 unless the same injected sequence is proven.

fix_assessment.rationale: A fix cannot be scoped until the pen dock event sequence and Keyboard Manager transformation are captured on supported Surface hardware.

issue_context.summary: Docking or undocking a Surface pen toggles Caps Lock and can invoke Screen Snip only when the CapsLock/Ctrl remap is enabled. The reporter reproduced on two Surface generations, and maintainers intentionally separated this false-action issue from the related remapping issue.
known_information: The failure occurs on pen removal and return.
The symptom persists across two Surface device generations.
The single-click pen action is no longer configured, yet Screen Snip can still appear.
Keyboard Manager disablement is a reliable negative control.
inferences: A synthetic or HID-generated key sequence associated with pen docking may pass through the CapsLock/Ctrl remap and become a Caps Lock toggle or Screen Snip chord.
Hardware/firmware differences may change the precise emitted sequence.
issue_context.analysis: The report is no longer waiting on the author: the author answered with a current device and a strong on/off control. Maintainer-side reproduction is the next action.
initial_investigation: Read the full body and all comments, including the maintainer distinction from issue 33968.
Reviewed the related issue URLs 23438 and 33968.
Identified KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary keyboard event handling and injected-event test infrastructure as the likely trace boundary without claiming a confirmed source cause.

actions.label: Trace Surface pen dock key events

reproduce.version_requirements: Current PowerToys on a Surface Laptop Studio or Surface Pro with a dockable pen
prerequisites: Configure a Caps Lock and Ctrl swap matching the report.
Record raw physical/HID and Keyboard Manager output events, including injected flags.
Verify the configured Windows pen click action before testing.
steps: Undock the pen and record Caps Lock state and all emitted key events.
Redock the pen and record Caps Lock state, Screen Snip activation, and emitted events.
Disable Keyboard Manager and repeat as the negative control.
Compare the sequence with the Win+Ctrl+F20 behavior tracked in issue 33968.
reproduce.expected_result: Pen docking and undocking must not toggle Caps Lock or invoke Screen Snip; the trace must show where Keyboard Manager changes the sequence.
